problems.title: The size of S
problems.statement: One attention head, sequence length N = 8,192, head dimension d = 128.

problems.title: Naive traffic versus flash traffic
problems.statement: Same head, FP32. Naive: read Q, K, V, write O, plus write S, read S, write P, read P. Flash (idealised): read Q, K, V once, write O.
hints: The N² terms dominate the naive version.
problems.solution: (a) 1040 MiB, (b) 16 MiB, (c) 65×. (Real FlashAttention re-reads K and V once per query block, so its traffic is $N/B_r$ times K and V; still far below N².)

problems.title: Intensity of the naive N² part
problems.statement: Naive attention's S and P traffic: about 16 bytes per score element (FP32 write S, read S, write P, read P), against 4d FLOPs per score (2d for QKᵀ, 2d for PV).
problems.solution: 16 and 32 FLOP/byte: below a tensor-core ridge of ~300 (H100 FP16). The "GEMM" workload is memory-bound because of S.

problems.title: The rescaling step
problems.statement: Running state (m, ℓ, o) = (2, 3.0, [1.5, 0.6]). The next key block has scores [4, 1] and value rows [1, 0] and [0, 1].
hints: ℓ ← αℓ + Σ e^{s_j − m'}; o ← αo + Σ e^{s_j − m'} v_j.
problems.solution: m' = 4, α = $e^{-2}$ = 0.1353. ℓ = 3α + $e^0$ + $e^{-3}$ = 1.4558. o₁ = 1.5α + 1·1 + $e^{-3}$·0 = 1.2030. Everything already accumulated is multiplied by α; the result is exact (a NumPy check of the full algorithm against direct softmax agrees to 1.1e-16).

problems.title: SRAM budget
problems.statement: A FlashAttention block holds a Q tile (B_r × d), K and V tiles (B_c × d each) and the score tile (B_r × B_c) on chip, FP16 operands, FP32 scores. d = 128.
hints: Q, K, V in FP16, S in FP32.
problems.solution: (a) 48 KB + 16 KB = 64 KB. (b) 96 KB + 64 KB = 160 KB: fits an H100 SM (228 KB) but not a 2060 Super (64 KB). Tile sizes follow the hardware's on-chip memory.

problems.title: Causal masking
problems.statement: Causal attention: query i attends to keys 0..i. Blocks of 128 on N = 8,192.

parts.prompt: Fraction of key blocks a query block must visit, on average?
Approximate speedup over computing the full square then masking?

hints: Query block i visits key blocks 0..i.
problems.solution: (a) $\sum_{i=1}^{64} i / 64^2 = 2080/4096 ≈ 0.51$. (b) ≈ 1.97×. Only the diagonal blocks need element-wise masks.

problems.title: Decode is different
problems.statement: Generation: one new query per step attends to N = 8,192 cached keys and values, d = 128, FP16.

parts.prompt: Bytes of K and V read per step?

problems.solution: (a) 4 MiB, (b) 4.2 MFLOP, (c) 1 FLOP/byte: pure bandwidth. Decode attention is a KV-cache streaming problem, which is why its kernels (FlashDecoding, paged attention) split the keys across blocks.

problems.title: Exact or approximate

options: mathematically exact; only rounding differs (summation order)

hints: Online softmax is an algebraic identity.
problems.solution: Exact: the rescaling reproduces softmax exactly. Differences are floating-point order effects, small and testable against a reference.

problems.title: Memory saved
problems.statement: Training a model with 32 heads, N = 4,096, batch 8, storing P (FP16) for the backward pass, versus FlashAttention recomputing it.

parts.prompt: GiB of P per layer stored naively?

problems.solution: 8 GiB per layer: impossible on most GPUs for many layers. FlashAttention stores only O and the row statistics (m, ℓ) and recomputes P in the backward pass: more FLOPs, far less memory, and faster overall.
